BATTER: A liquid or semiliquid mixture, as of flour, eggs, and milk, used in cooking.
BLUEBERRY: Sweet edible dark-blue berries of either low-growing or high-growing blueberry plants.
BOLOGNA: Large smooth-textured smoked sausage of beef and veal and pork.
BURGER: A sandwich consisting of a fried cake of minced beef served on a bun, often with other ingredients.
CABBAGE: A vegetable with a dense head of green, white or red leaves.
CAKE: A sweet baked food made from flour, sugar, eggs and fat.
CHERRY: A red fruit with a single hard stone.
CHESTNUT: Edible nut of any of various chestnut trees of the genus Castanea.
COBBLER: A baked fruit dessert with a thick, scone-like topping.
CRAB: The edible flesh of any of various crabs.
CRANBERRY: Very tart red berry used for sauce or juice.
CREAM: The part of milk containing the butterfat.
CRUMBLE: A baked dessert of fruit under a crumbly topping of flour, butter and sugar.
GUMBO: A thick Creole stew of meat or seafood, thickened with okra.
HOTDOG: A frankfurter served hot on a bun.
LETTUCE: Leaves of any of various plants of Lactuca sativa.
LIME: The green acidic fruit of any of various lime trees.
MACARONI: Pasta in the form of slender tubes.
MOCHA: A flavoring made from coffee mixed with chocolate.
MUSTARD: Pungent powder or paste prepared from ground mustard seeds.
NACHOS: A tortilla chip topped with cheese and chili-pepper and broiled.
OLIVE: One-seeded fruit of the European olive tree usually pickled and used as a relish.
ORANGE: Round yellow to orange fruit of any of several citrus trees.
OREGANO: Pungent leaves used as seasoning with meats and fowl and in stews and soups and omelets.
OYSTER: Edible body of any of numerous oysters.
PAPAYA: Large oval melon-like tropical fruit with yellowish flesh.
PEACH: Downy juicy fruit with sweet yellowish or whitish flesh.
PECAN: Smooth brown oval nut of south central United States.
PEPPER: Pungent seasoning from the berry of the common pepper plant of East India; use whole or ground.
PLANTAIN: Starchy banana-like fruit; eaten as a staple vegetable throughout the tropics.
PLUM: A small round fruit with smooth purple, red or yellow skin and a stone.
QUICHE: A tart filled with rich unsweetened custard; often contains other ingredients.
ROSEMARY: Extremely pungent leaves used fresh or dried as seasoning for especially meats.
SCALLOP: Edible muscle of mollusks having fan-shaped shells.
SHRIMP: Any of various edible decapod crustaceans.
SMOOTHIE: A thick smooth drink consisting of fresh fruit pureed with ice cream or yoghurt or milk.
SPRINKLES: Bits of sweet chocolate used as a topping on e.g. ice cream.
SQUASH: Edible fruit of a squash plant; eaten as a vegetable.
STEW: Food prepared by stewing especially meat or fish with vegetables.
STOCK: Liquid in which meat and vegetables are simmered; used as a basis for e.g. soups or sauces.
STUFFING: A mixture of seasoned ingredients used to stuff meats and vegetables.
TAMALE: Corn and cornmeal dough stuffed with a meat mixture then wrapped in corn husks and steamed.
TAMARIND: Large tropical seed pod with very tangy pulp that is eaten fresh or cooked.
TART: A small open pie with a fruit filling.
TARTAR: A sauce of mayonnaise with chopped pickles and capers, served with fish.
TUNA: Important warm-water fatty fish of the genus Thunnus of the family Scombridae.
TURMERIC: Ground dried rhizome of the turmeric plant used as seasoning.
VANILLA: A flavoring prepared from vanilla beans macerated in alcohol.
